search_strategy: Systematic and multi-surface, but keyword-bound. The agent worked Gitea (fetched all 550 issues+PRs locally, grepped titles/bodies for attachment/multimodal/mime keywords, then pulled full body+comments for ~15 relevant numbers — found only background, no design detail), BookStack (tried /api/search for 'attachment'/'mime'/'AttachmentBlock' — zero hits, correctly recognized this as the comments-not-indexed trap and instead fetched all 228 pages WITH their comments to a local dump and grepped — still found nothing wiki-side except generic 'multimodal' status mentions), IMAP mail (searched all 107 messages for the same terms — 'attachment'/'mime'/'AttachmentBlock' zero hits, 'multimodal' 12 hits, all release/weekly-update boilerplate), and Mattermost (logged in, ran a targeted multi-term search first, then escalated to dumping ALL 10,304 posts across 12 channels to a local chronological file and grepping with widening context windows — three successive passes with different seed vocabularies: 'attachment|fingerprint|size_mb|ceiling|oversize|MB|mime|filename', then 'attachment|mime|_canonical|render|block', then the tightest and most effective, 'attachment|sha256|size_mb|oversiz|too large|_canonical' with ±8/+16 line windows). This last pass, plus several earlier `sed -n '1,40p' /tmp/chat.txt`-style dumps of direct multi-term chat searches, is what surfaced the bulk of the 51 remarks (39 of 51, 76%). The failure mode is structural: coverage was keyed to a fixed, if well-chosen, vocabulary (attachment/mime/fingerprint/ceiling/filename/detail/_canonical/too large/MB/sha256/IMAGE_DETAILS/tokens), so any remark phrased without one of those tokens was invisible regardless of how many surrounding lines were dumped — 12 of 51 remarks were never surfaced at all (verified individually by grep across the full transcript), and one more (g8.r2.rev1) was seen only as a single out-of-context line because it happened to also contain the unrelated word 'render' that a later, differently-purposed grep was searching for. Critically, the missed remarks are not randomly distributed: three of the six failure_behavior remarks for r2 (rev1, l15, l16) all carry the same specific fact — 'warn exactly once on fallback' — and all three were missed by different mechanisms (decontextualized single-line hit, and two complete misses), which is why that fact was never recovered despite the agent otherwise correctly reconstructing the rest of the detail-normalization design (vocabulary, case-folding, fallback value, no mutation of Image.detail).
end_reason: Full completion, not a partial/dead run. The agent cloned the repo, read all relevant code, gathered context from Gitea/BookStack/mail/Mattermost, wrote the canonical attachment.py module and patched all four request-processor files, wrote and iterated its own 25-test unit suite to green (catching and fixing an abstract-method stub bug, a pydantic validate_default bug, and the prompt-total/hook ordering bug against its own tests), pushed to a feature branch, opened/merged the PR, and confirmed CI run #3 for commit f196f277 green and the running curator service healthy before marking task_complete. provenance.pushed=1, provenance.ci_green=1, provenance.deployed=1, g8.suite_ok=1 all confirm this. The two lost facts (g8.r1.rule, g8.r2.failure_behavior) are pure requirement-recovery misses/slips, not infrastructure or run-termination issues.
notable: The agent's own grep vocabulary, not corpus placement, is the direct cause of missing 12/51 remarks — every miss was checked individually and confirmed to have zero hits anywhere in the 7847-line transcript, i.e. the information was genuinely never displayed to the model, not just skimmed.

g8.r1.rule's failure is a real implementation bug the agent could plausibly have caught with more thorough self-testing: its own 25 unit tests all passed, but none of them exercised the single-block path (`_canonical_attachment_block` in isolation) with a document exactly at the 24.0 MB ceiling and a hook that raises — the exact scenario the grader's oracle test uses (transcript lines 6683-6838, agent's test failures were all TypeErrors/setup bugs, never a ceiling-boundary case).

g8.r2.failure_behavior's failure traces to a single grep call (searching for the renderer seam keyword 'render') that incidentally surfaced one line of the one remark (rev1) that states the warning requirement, and the agent never re-fetched the surrounding context of that hit — a case where reading strategy (single-line grep matches, not always followed up with wider context) rather than corpus coverage caused the miss, since the seed vocabulary used elsewhere ('IMAGE_DETAILS', 'detail', 'auto') would very plausibly have caught l16's 'log that once' had that specific window been re-grepped.

This is a genuinely difficult task-generation edge case worth flagging: g8.r2.rev1 is the ONLY remark among l13/l14/l15/l16/fix24/rev1/rev2 that states the exact fact the grader tests ('one warning ... falls back to auto'); the other five, despite all being tagged failure_behavior and several being found by the agent, do not individually supply this fact even when read in full (rev2 and l14 describe the normalization mechanism but not the logging; l13 describes only the incident; fix24 is about tuple ordering, not warnings).
